clue.text: Expert involved in case study as girl put on weight

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece put on another follows it, so the girl's name comes after the weight

parts.note: a gram is a small unit of weight
Marian is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl gaining weight is somehow linked with an expert busy on a case study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case study' sounds like law or medicine, but it means the study of grammatical cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammarian is a scholar of grammar, which includes the study of noun cases.

clue.text: Facility provided in great setting

indicators.note: the abbreviation for great forms a setting around the conditional word

parts.note: Gt is the standard abbreviation for Great in place names such as Gt Yarmouth
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Some convenience is offered in grand surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facility' means a natural talent here, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A facility for something is a natural talent or knack for it.

clue.text: A poet I found acceptable without any evidence

parts.note: taken as written
Matthew Prior was an English poet of the early 1700s
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone approves of a poet without needing proof.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew Prior was an English poet and diplomat.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning from first principles rather than observation is accepted before experience, without evidence.

clue.text: You may see lob used in these

definitions.text: You may see lob used in these

parts.note: these two words are a jumble of the second word of the answer, with the first word acting as the anagram signal

explanation.surface: Tennis matches where lobs get played.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken as tennis, a lob is a high shot used in men-and-women pairs matches; taken cryptically, LOB USED is DOUBLES mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis played by pairs each made up of a man and a woman, where lobs are common.

clue.text: Acted in violent fashion to swindle the elderly

parts.note: a ramp is British slang for a swindle or racket
the aged are old people

explanation.surface: Someone behaved violently to cheat old people.
explanation.walkthrough: RAMP is British slang for a swindle or racket.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about wildly and violently.

clue.text: In a period of prosperity pound is flourishing

indicators.note: the pound sign goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a boom is a time of economic growth
L stands for the pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: In good economic times the currency is thriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money in a sentence about economics, and it is: its symbol L goes into A BOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in flower means blossoming, a picture of flourishing.

clue.text: Extremities of trout visible in river

explanation.surface: An angler spots the tail and nose of a fish in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The word trout begins and ends with the letter T, so its extremities are two T's, spelt out as a word. 'Visible in' only links the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelt-out letters: the first and last letters of trout are both T; separately, the Tees is a river in north-east England.

clue.text: Support for flower power?

parts.note: the flower of society is its choicest part, so backing rule by that select group is meant, not hippy pacifism

explanation.surface: Backing for the 1960s hippy movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower power' suggests hippies, but 'flower' means the elite, the best of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism is belief in rule or dominance by a select, superior few.

clue.text: Drinks party creates a little work

parts.note: shorts are measures of spirits
the Tory party is Britain's Conservative party

explanation.surface: A drinks party results in a small piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: SHORTS are small measures of spirits; TORY is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief prose fiction is a small literary work.

clue.text: Times given quite enough warning in advance, say

indicators.note: puts the warning piece in front of the other two

parts.note: golfers shout fore as a warning
X is the multiplication sign, read as times
ample means plenty, quite enough

explanation.surface: Someone is told, well beforehand, more than once, what is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Say' used before an instance means the same as giving an instance, as in 'pick a colour, say blue'.

clue.text: Something available from shelf in off-licence

indicators.note: available from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shopper finds an item on the shelf of a British off-licence, a shop selling alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: The vague 'Something' is the definition: the whole clue hints that this is a drink found in an off-licence.
explanation.definitionFit: Fino is a pale dry sherry, the kind of thing stocked in a shop selling alcohol, so 'Something' covers it loosely.

clue.text: Press crew covering the country

indicators.note: in a down clue the crew sits on top of the rest

parts.note: a four is a rowing boat crewed by four
taken as written
a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: Journalists are working across the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: A FOUR is a rowing crew; the answer is journalism's traditional nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalism, the newspapers collectively, has long been called this, after the three estates of the realm.

clue.text: Playwright's part in The Merry Wives of Windsor

definitions.text: part in The Merry Wives of Windsor

explanation.surface: Asks about one role in a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: John Ford was a Jacobean dramatist; Master Ford is a jealous husband in Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Two names: the dramatist John Ford, and Master Ford, a character in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Defender in a game getting essential point

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist of something is its essential point

explanation.surface: A defender in a sport is getting to the heart of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defender' looks like a sports position, but it means someone defending a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist argues in defence of a belief or cause.

clue.text: Aggressive kick that leaves receiver facing a charge

definitions.text: Aggressive kick that leaves receiver facing a charge

parts.words: Aggressive kick that leaves receiver facing a charge
parts.note: in rugby, a very high punt hangs long enough for the kicker's team to rush the player waiting to catch it

explanation.surface: Sounds like a blow leaving someone receiving stolen goods facing prosecution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' and 'charge' suggest crime, but this is a rugby kick: the catcher faces a charge of oncoming players.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby high kick, the Garryowen, chased so the catcher is tackled on landing.

clue.text: Misbehaving person state's put inside

indicators.note: says the state's letters go inside the rearranged word
the word person behaves badly, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
RI is the abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island

explanation.surface: Someone who misbehaves gets locked up by the state.
explanation.walkthrough: RI is the US state of Rhode Island. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: someone who misbehaves is locked up by the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone jailed by the state for misbehaving is an inmate of a jail.

clue.text: Careless playing in part could result in this

definitions.text: Careless playing in part could result in this

parts.words: Careless playing in part could result in this
parts.note: an actor who plays a role carelessly and forgets the lines needs a whispered cue from the wings

explanation.surface: Sloppy performance in a role leads to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' and 'part' suggest music, but they mean acting a role.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue given to an actor who has forgotten the lines, as a careless performer might need.

clue.text: Editor held up by sticky problem in newspaper section

indicators.note: the turned letters are held within the other letters
the word sticky is a problem, so its letters are rearranged
in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top

explanation.surface: An editor is delayed by an awkward difficulty in a section of the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Editor held up' reads as a delayed journalist, but 'up' turns the abbreviation in this down clue and 'held' puts it inside the rearranged letters of the word that 'problem' jumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A city desk is the department of a newspaper handling local or financial news.

clue.text: Result of injury to, say. Ben Battle

indicators.note: an injury damages the following words, so the letters of say and Ben are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ben has been hurt in a fight, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: Naseby was a decisive battle of the English Civil War in 1645.
explanation.definitionFit: Naseby is the Northamptonshire village where Parliament's army beat the Royalists in 1645, a famous battle.

clue.text: Painter not so well taught at first

parts.note: sicker means more ill, less well

indicators.note: only the opening letter of taught is used

explanation.surface: An artist whose health was poor learned early on.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Sickert was an English painter of the Camden Town Group.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Sickert was a British artist, so he is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Man near rook said to disturb the bird

indicators.note: the chess piece is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same without the K

parts.note: on a chessboard the knight is the man standing next to the rook at the start
to jar is to jolt or disturb

explanation.surface: A fellow beside a crow is reported to upset a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece: at the start the knight stands beside the rook. 'Rook' tempts as the bird itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal bird known for its churring call.

clue.text: Bloomer in second of March issue over new writer, say

annotationWithheld.why: Bloomer in second of March issue over new writer, say: JO (second of the March children in Little Women) + N + QUILL gives one L too many for JONQUIL, and no word removes it
annotationWithheld.clue: Bloomer in second of March issue over new writer, say

clue.text: Duke's about to hide at home

annotationWithheld.why: Duke's about to hide at home: ORSINO is the duke in Twelfth Night, but no reading of about / to hide / at home (IN) builds ORS-IN-O
annotationWithheld.clue: Duke's about to hide at home

clue.text: A relation of 25 in an obscure way

explanation.surface: A relative of a king acts in a vague manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is LEAR, here Edward Lear, whose poem 'Incidents in the Life of my Uncle Arly' names this relation.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Arly is a character in a poem by the nonsense writer; separately, the word means vaguely or without clarity.

clue.text: Polish friend of Chopin

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a Polish companion of the composer Chopin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, which suits Chopin, but it is the verb meaning to smooth. George Sand, the French novelist, was Chopin's lover.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooth a surface with abrasive is to polish it; George Sand was the novelist who was the composer's partner.

clue.text: King Edward

explanation.surface: Names a British monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear is Shakespeare's king and Edward Lear the nonsense poet; the surface suggests one of England's King Edwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic monarch is King Lear, and Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse.

clue.text: Affair at which one may find satisfaction with a second helping

definitions.text: Affair at which one may find satisfaction with a second helping

parts.words: Affair at which one may find satisfaction with a second helping
parts.note: a gentleman demanding satisfaction for an insult fights a formal combat, assisted by a second

explanation.surface: Sounds like a meal where a second plate leaves one satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satisfaction' and 'second' sound like food, but a second is a duellist's assistant and satisfaction is honour restored.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal fight to settle a point of honour, where each party is attended by a second.

clue.text: Collectively writing volume about a true original

indicators.note: the volume goes around the other letters

parts.note: a litre is a measure of volume

indicators.note: the letters of a and true are made new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Writing a book about something genuinely unique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' is an unusual anagram signal: something original is new, so the letters are made anew as ERATU, which 'about' places inside the volume measure after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Written works taken as a whole are called literature.

clue.text: Deserve censure

explanation.surface: Merit a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate is to merit, as in 'rate a mention', and also, in older use, to scold someone angrily.

clue.text: Work's bound to become available in his business

definitions.text: Work's bound to become available in his business

parts.words: Work's bound to become available in his business
parts.note: a written work, once bound, goes on sale in a shop selling printed volumes

explanation.surface: A job is sure to turn up in someone's trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' and 'bound' look like employment and certainty, but a work is a book and bound means given covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer whose trade is selling printed volumes.
